headword: {工業革命|こうぎょうかくめい}

definitions.explanation: The historical transformation, beginning in 18th-century Britain, in which manufacturing shifted from hand production to machines, factories, and mechanized industry.

examples.japanese: {工業革命|こうぎょうかくめい}について{学|まな}ぶ。
{工業革命|こうぎょうかくめい}はイギリスで{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain.

examples.japanese: {工業革命|こうぎょうかくめい}によって{人々|ひとびと}の{暮|く}らしや{働|はたら}き{方|かた}が{大|おお}きく{変|か}わった。
examples.english: The Industrial Revolution greatly changed how people lived and worked.

notes:
Formed from {工業|こうぎょう} (industry, manufacturing) + {革命|かくめい} (revolution). A standard term in history and social-studies education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {産業革命|さんぎょうかくめい}: the Industrial Revolution (the more common synonym)
- {第|だい}{四次|よじ}{産業革命|さんぎょうかくめい}: the Fourth Industrial Revolution

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {産業革命|さんぎょうかくめい}: Industrial Revolution — the more widely used term in Japanese textbooks; {工業革命|こうぎょうかくめい} stresses the shift to factory manufacturing specifically
- {技術革新|ぎじゅつかくしん}: technological innovation — refers to advances in technology in general, not the specific historical event
